title: cgroup hierarchy issue with WSL 3.0.1
body:
### Issue Description

Seems a new incompatibility has been introduced with the release of WSL 3.0.1 (installed automatically on my machine yesterday morning).  Since that install, when I run 
`podman compose up -d` 
I get something like this:
`Error response from daemon: crun: controller `pids` is not available under /sys/fs/cgroup/non-systemd/machine.slice/libpod-d2468754a3354cb9676d2f676428a324526467ef592b3fb0a91737fbb41d7491.scope/container/cgroup.controllers: OCI runtime error`

A simpler test is described in "Steps to reproduce" below.

Main things tried so far: 

- Stopped/started podman machine (podman-machine-default)
- Updated Podman from 6.1.2 to 6.1.3
- Deleted containers
- Deleted images, pulled them back down
- Used CoPilot to help diagnose (lots of steps)
- Recreated podman-machine-default


### Steps to reproduce the issue

Run these commands in PowerShell or Git Bash.
1. `podman machine start`
2. `podman run --rm alpine echo hello`



### Describe the results you received

Something like this, though the container ID changes. 
`Error: preparing container cde1d3955a029f52fdc94ba1e944661dfb472554d7e7d3b0d0c8808663a673d1 for attach: crun: controller `pids` is not available under /sys/fs/cgroup/non-systemd/user.slice/user-1000.slice/user@1000.service/user.slice/libpod-cde1d3955a029f52fdc94ba1e944661dfb472554d7e7d3b0d0c8808663a673d1.scope/container/cgroup.controllers: OCI runtime error`

### Describe the results you expected

The text `hello`

comments.body:
I have also started seeing errors immediately following the WSL 3.0.1 update. I get the same error cfframe reported when running `podman run --rm alpine echo hello`. I see a different error when running `podman-compose up`:

> Error: unable to start container XYZ: preparing container XYX for attach: unable to create pod cgroup for pod PDQ: creating cgroup user.slice/user-1000.slice/user@1000.service/user.slice/user-libpod_pod_PDQ.slice: Unit user-libpod_pod_PDQ.slice was already loaded or has a fragment file.

where XYZ and PDQ are the respective container and pod hex strings.

Example compose.yml (same error with any compose file):
```
services:
  svc:
    image: 'alpine:latest'
```

I have the exact same versions of WSL and Podman as cfframe.

I've tried deleting and recreating the Podman Machine rootful, rootless, and with/without user-mode networking enabled, using Podman Desktop v1.29.3 with no change in results.
We already have a fix that should land in the next release, see https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29749 for workarounds until then
